scenes.tts: One mouse scratches normally to histamine, yet scratches much less to chloroquine. Did one experiment separate two neurons, or only two inputs? Watch one skin-to-cord pathway. Gold histamine and blue chloroquine approach the same teal sensory population.
scenes.caption: One mouse scratches normally to histamine, yet scratches much less to chloroquine. Did one experiment separate two neurons, or only two inputs? Watch one skin-to-cord pathway. Gold histamine and blue chloroquine approach the same teal sensory population.
scenes.visual: Hook first. Fill the frame with a skin cross-section, teal sensory endings, and a cord at right. Gold histamine and blue chloroquine droplets travel toward the same endings. A small title, Which Line Carries the Itch?, appears only after the two questions. Colour map for both chapters: histamine gold, chloroquine blue, itch-route neurons teal, pain-related output red, inhibition purple, neutral tissue white. Keep particles moving.
scenes.narration: One mouse scratches normally to histamine, yet scratches much less to chloroquine. Did one experiment separate two neurons, or only two inputs? Watch one skin-to-cord pathway. Gold histamine and blue chloroquine approach the same teal sensory population.

scenes.tts: Researchers deleted one cluster of M R G P R receptor genes. The blue chloroquine route broke, so scratching fell. Gold histamine scratching remained. The intervention separated receptor routes. It did not yet separate the neurons carrying them.
scenes.caption: Researchers deleted one cluster of Mrgpr receptor genes. The blue chloroquine route broke, so scratching fell. Gold histamine scratching remained. The intervention separated receptor routes. It did not yet separate the neurons carrying them.
scenes.visual: Carry the same cross-section. Enlarge one teal ending. Remove a blue Mrgpr receptor block from its membrane; the blue arrow dissolves before reaching a schematic scratching gauge. Keep the gold arrow moving through a separate gold receptor block. Label the response gauges schematic.
scenes.narration: Researchers deleted one cluster of Mrgpr receptor genes. The blue chloroquine route broke, so scratching fell. Gold histamine scratching remained. The intervention separated receptor routes. It did not yet separate the neurons carrying them.

scenes.tts: The routes also recruit different channel machinery in mice. Histamine itch involves P L C beta three and T R P V one. Chloroquine and B A M eight twenty-two scratching instead falls markedly without T R P A one.
scenes.caption: The routes also recruit different channel machinery in mice. Histamine itch involves PLC-beta-3 and TRPV1. Chloroquine and BAM8-22 scratching instead falls markedly without TRPA1.
scenes.visual: Keep both inputs on the same enlarged ending. The gold path turns a PLC-beta-3 cog and opens a TRPV1 block. The blue path and a second BAM8-22 chip converge on a TRPA1 block. Remove TRPA1 and lower a shared chloroquine-and-BAM8-22 schematic gauge; leave the gold path visible without assigning it an outcome in this experiment.
scenes.narration: The routes also recruit different channel machinery in mice. Histamine itch involves PLC-beta-3 and TRPV1. Chloroquine and BAM8-22 scratching instead falls markedly without TRPA1.

scenes.tts: Now remove every sensory neuron marked by M R G P R A three. What should happen to histamine scratching? Predict before the cells disappear. Does the gold route survive, as it did before?
scenes.caption: Now remove every sensory neuron marked by MrgprA3. What should happen to histamine scratching? Predict before the cells disappear. Does the gold route survive, as it did before?
scenes.visual: Zoom to the teal MrgprA3-marked population, still receiving both coloured arrows. A large question overlays the intact cells: Will histamine scratching remain? The gold route pulses slowly while a dotted outline previews cell removal.
scenes.narration: Now remove every sensory neuron marked by MrgprA3. What should happen to histamine scratching? Predict before the cells disappear. Does the gold route survive, as it did before?

scenes.visual: Hold the prediction question for 4.5 seconds. Keep only slow gold flow and gentle membrane motion; reveal no answer.

scenes.tts: Histamine scratching also fell. Removing a receptor route and removing its whole neuron population are different interventions. The neurons receive several itch-producing inputs. Ablation shows they are needed for much scratching in these mouse assays.
scenes.caption: Histamine scratching also fell. Removing a receptor route and removing its whole neuron population are different interventions. The neurons receive several itch-producing inputs. Ablation shows they are needed for much scratching in these mouse assays.
scenes.visual: The teal cells fade completely, taking both gold and blue paths with them. Both schematic scratching gauges fall. Transform two small labels beneath the same picture: receptor deletion means one input lost; cell ablation means every input through that population lost.
scenes.narration: Histamine scratching also fell. Removing a receptor route and removing its whole neuron population are different interventions. The neurons receive several itch-producing inputs. Ablation shows they are needed for much scratching in these mouse assays.

scenes.tts: A second test started with mice lacking working T R P V one. Researchers restored that channel only in the teal neurons. Capsaicin could now recruit only that population. The mouse produced itch-related behaviour instead of its usual pain-related wiping.
scenes.caption: A second test started with mice lacking working TRPV1. Researchers restored that channel only in the teal neurons. Capsaicin could now recruit only that population. The mouse produced itch-related behaviour instead of its usual pain-related wiping.
scenes.visual: Rebuild the teal population in the same place. All TRPV1 slots begin empty, while other channels stay in place. Insert one labelled TRPV1 block only into teal cells. A capsaicin drop enters through that block. At right, transform a red forepaw-wipe icon into a teal hindpaw-scratch icon.
scenes.narration: A second test started with mice lacking working TRPV1. Researchers restored that channel only in the teal neurons. Capsaicin could now recruit only that population. The mouse produced itch-related behaviour instead of its usual pain-related wiping.

scenes.tts: The rescue shows what these neurons can drive when they alone respond to capsaicin. It does not prove every activation means itch. Later, fast ionotropic stimulation mostly evoked pain-related defence. G Q linked stimulation evoked itch behaviour.
scenes.caption: The rescue shows what these neurons can drive when they alone respond to capsaicin. It does not prove every activation means itch. Later, fast ionotropic stimulation mostly evoked pain-related defence. Gq-linked stimulation evoked itch behaviour.
scenes.visual: Keep one teal neuron. Split its input into two animated controls: a fast switch drives a red defensive-output gauge; a slower Gq dial drives a teal scratching gauge. Mark both gauges schematic. A strict ITCH ONLY stamp appears, then cracks.
scenes.narration: The rescue shows what these neurons can drive when they alone respond to capsaicin. It does not prove every activation means itch. Later, fast ionotropic stimulation mostly evoked pain-related defence. Gq-linked stimulation evoked itch behaviour.

scenes.tts: Behaviour matters too. In the cheek assay, hindpaw scratching counts as itch-related output. Forelimb wiping counts as pain-related output. Those readouts distinguish actions, not a mouse's reported sensation. Human M R G P R X one is also a different gene.
scenes.caption: Behaviour matters too. In the cheek assay, hindpaw scratching counts as itch-related output. Forelimb wiping counts as pain-related output. Those readouts distinguish actions, not a mouse's reported sensation. Human MRGPRX1 is also a different gene.
scenes.visual: Pull back to a large mouse head and forelimbs. Animate one hindpaw scratch and one forelimb wipe in separate lanes. Replace the mouse gene label MrgprA3 with a non-equal sign and human MRGPRX1; do not draw a human neuron lineage.
scenes.narration: Behaviour matters too. In the cheek assay, hindpaw scratching counts as itch-related output. Forelimb wiping counts as pain-related output. Those readouts distinguish actions, not a mouse's reported sensation. Human MRGPRX1 is also a different gene.

scenes.tts: Both receptors respond to chloroquine in transfected cells, but not equally. The human receptor's functional potency was lower in that assay. Shared ligand responses do not make the genes, neurons, or sensations equivalent across species.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule for this lesson. Trigger, recruited population, spinal route, and inhibition together shape scratching. Each perturbation supports only the link it tests. Chapter two will carry this pathway into the spinal cord.
